book.title: Career and Technical Education Grade 7 Student Textbook
book.subject: cte

title: How to develop a personal profile

keywords.def: Detailed information about a specific person: who they are and what they have.
Short and clear, with only the important points.

ideas.name: Three steps to write a profile

en.text: Write a personal profile in order and briefly. Step 1: describe yourself: name, address, age. Step 2: mention your skills and abilities. Step 3: include your education and experience. A profile for a job must be short and focus on what the job needs.

screens.title: Short or long?
screens.ask: Which profile is easier for an employer to read quickly?
opts: A short one with the important points
A ten-page story of your life
screens.after: Employers read many profiles. A short, focused profile is best.

screens.title: 2.3.2 How to develop a personal profile
paras: A personal profile is written in order and briefly.
It focuses on your most important attributes.

screens.title: The three steps
steps: Give a brief description of yourself: name, address, age, sex. Address: region, zone, woreda, town, school.
Mention your skills and abilities: translating, speaking a language, knitting, drawing. Add statements like "I am hard working and cooperative."
Include education or experience: for example "Grade 7". Voluntary work counts too, if the profile is for a job.

screens.title: For a job
paras: A profile for a job should be short and concise.
Then it can be read quickly.
It focuses on what is linked to the specific job.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Short and clear, with only the important points.

screens.why: This is the order the book gives.

items: I live in Adama, Oromia Region.
I can speak Afaan Oromo, Amharic and English.
I am hard working and cooperative.
I volunteered in a school cleaning campaign.
screens.why: Description, then skills, then education or experience.
screens.clue: Is the line about who you are, what you can do, or what you have done?

screens.text: Information to be included in a personal profile for a job is:
screens.why: Name and address, skills, and education or experience all belong.

screens.text: Voluntary work cannot go in a profile for a job.
screens.why: Any experience, even voluntary, can be included for a job.

screens.text: Sara writes a profile for a job at a computer shop. Which line should she put first?
opts: "My name is Sara Bekele. I live in Hawassa and I am in Grade 7."
screens.ans: "My name is Sara Bekele. I live in Hawassa and I am in Grade 7."
screens.why: Step 1 is a brief description of yourself. Skills and experience come after.

items: My name is Abebe Kebede. I live in Adama.
I speak three languages and I am good at drawing.
I completed Grade 6 and helped in a carpentry workshop.
items.why: A profile goes: about you, skills, then education or experience.

test.text: What is the first step in writing a personal profile?
opts: Give a brief description of yourself
test.ans: Give a brief description of yourself
test.why: Step 1 is about who you are.

test.text: A profile for a job should be short and concise.
test.why: So it can be read quickly.

test.ask: Step 2 of a profile: mention your skills and ___.

test.text: "I am hard working and diligent." Which step does this belong to?
Which profile line is best for a job as a tailor?
opts: "I sewed school uniforms in my mother's shop."
test.ans: "I sewed school uniforms in my mother's shop."
test.why: A job profile focuses on what the job needs.

notes.text: Activity 10 asks students to write their own profile; the lesson turns it into ordering three model lines. Teachers can still ask for a written profile.
